_comment: THE HYDROGEN CANDIDATE LIST, machine-readable so the gap can be REPORTED rather
than narrated. sources/report_candidate_gaps.py reads it and prints what is still
missing on every build. Same shape and same purpose as sources/batteries_candidates.json.
WHAT THE PERIMETER ADMITS AND WHAT IT CANNOT YET HOLD. Brief 7 admits an electrolytic
hydrogen production project at or above 100 MW of electrolyser capacity on a
company-confirmed site. Every entry below clears that bar: a company source names the
site and states a figure at or above the threshold. What most of them do not yet have
is a POSITION, and the perimeter's other half — every site carries a latitude and a
longitude from a quoted source — is what keeps them here rather than in
data/transition/projects.json.
AND THAT IS THE FINDING OF THIS PASS, not a defect in it. Batteries stalled on company
confirmation: the sweep found sites the operator had never named. Hydrogen stalls
somewhere else entirely. The companies name their sites plainly and publish the
megawatts; what is missing is that these works mostly DO NOT EXIST YET. They are
construction fields inside refineries and chemical parks, and OpenStreetMap has drawn
two of them. The binding constraint on this dataset is the basemap's coverage of
buildings that are not built.
`coordinate_source` is one of the values in sector_map.LOCATION_SOURCE_TYPES or null.
Null means outstanding, and outstanding is the thing this file is for. Where a
position was looked for and not found, `coordinate_ref` says where it was looked for,
so the next person does not repeat the search.
`capacity_mw_input` is the electrolyser figure the company states, in MW of electrical
input, and is null where the company states the project in another unit only —
hoest-ptx-esbjerg is the case. Never converted. See sources/scope.md, 'Three units for
one electrolyser, and no conversion between them'.
REFUSALS ARE NOT HERE. This file is the admitted set; what the perimeter refuses, and
why, is in sources/hydrogen_docket.md, which is the reviewed record. The one exception
the brief names is blue hydrogen, which goes to candidates with a reason rather than to
refusals, because the class is a ruling George has not made yet.
`benchmarks` CARRIES THE EXTERNAL IDS FOR CANDIDATES TOO, not only for rows. The brief asks
the benchmark file to compare every admitted row, candidate and refusal, and a candidate whose
id lived only in a row would drop out of the comparison at exactly the point the comparison is
most interesting: eufabric holds thirteen sites the outside lists also hold, and cannot draw
them. null means the list was searched and the site is not in it.
UPDATED 9 SEPTEMBER 2026, AFTER THE HOST-WORKS RULING. Three entries left this list by
becoming rows on it — Hamburg Green Hydrogen Hub onto a dead coal station, Uniper onto its
own power station, Repsol onto its Tarragona refinery. Nothing was deleted: the entries stay
as the record of what was needed, and report_candidate_gaps stops asking for them.
THE TEN THAT REMAIN NOW WAIT ON SOMETHING DIFFERENT. Before the ruling they waited on a
polygon of the installation. Now they wait on a polygon of anything that is a WORKS rather
than an ESTATE — and an industrial park, a port and a business park are all estates, refused
on the rule Subotica and Mo i Rana settled. The note on each says which of the two it is.
THE LIST IS AT ITS END, 9 SEPTEMBER 2026. All twenty candidates are rows. Ten came in on
their own or a host works; ten came in on the ruling that POSITION IS NOT AN ADMISSION LEG,
carrying location_precision "none" and, on the row itself, the sweep that failed to place
them. `coordinate_source: "none"` on those ten is the same fact from this file's side.
NOTHING IS DELETED. Each entry stays as the record of what was needed and what was found,
and report_candidate_gaps prints 20 of 20 rather than asking for anything. The file is now a
history of a docket rather than a queue, which is what a finished docket looks like.
TWO ENTRIES ADDED 9 SEPTEMBER 2026 BY THE BENCHMARK GAP REPORT, not by the perimeter sweep.
sources/report_benchmark_gap.py classifies every European entry at or above 100 MW in either
outside list that this register does not hold, and its `not searched` class is the only one
that is a defect: an entry at FID or beyond, in the geography, above the threshold, that
nothing here explains. It found four. Two are the phases of one project, Gigastack; one is
INEOS Köln; one is Centurion, refused in the docket. Both admitted ones are now rows.
THIS IS THE DISCOVERY ROUTE THE BATTERIES FILE PREDICTED. That file noted that the funding
trail found two candidates the sweep had missed. The benchmark trail is the second such route
and it is better, because it is exhaustive over a published list and it can be re-run.

candidates.note: THE AMMONIA CASE, AND THE NO-MEGAWATTS CASE. The project's own site states no MW at all: 'HØST PtX Esbjerg will use renewable resources to produce approx. 100.000 tonnes of green hydrogen' and 'Expected annual production of 600,000 t green ammonia'. Both are recorded as stated, neither is converted, and the row will carry t_h2_per_year as its lead figure because MW input is absent. TRANSITION IS decarbonisation AND NOT THE AMMONIA DEFAULT: the brief's default is supply_security unless the source states decarbonisation, and this source does — 'By producing green hydrogen and ammonia, HØST PtX Esbjerg will open the door to decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors'.

candidates.note: THE ATTRITION CASE THIS SECTOR NEEDS, and the one candidate here with a stop on its record. HH2E filed for insolvency in December 2024 after its majority shareholder declined further financing — stop_reason `finance` — and its own website now refuses a connection outright, which is why nothing on this entry cites hh2e.de. H2APEX Nova Holding became sole owner of HH2E Werk Lubmin GmbH on 2 July 2025 through a completed insolvency plan procedure, an OWNERSHIP event, and states '100 MW plant in the first expansion stage by 2028'.
